fields.h1: Build an Equipment Rental Agreement Form Renters Sign at Pickup
fields.hero_description: Tell Emergent what you rent and on what terms. It builds the equipment rental agreement form, logs each item's serial number and condition, and keeps every rental in one table.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Equipment Rental Agreement Form
fields.features_heading: What the Agreement Records for Each Rental
fields.features_subheading: A template leaves a blank for each term. The form fills them from the renter's answers and keeps the record once the gear is back.
fields.feature_1:
Each item named by its serial number

Emergent lists every item on the agreement with its serial number and what it costs to replace. A renter taking two generators signs for two serial numbers, not one vague line.
fields.feature_2:
Daily and weekly rates per item

Give each item a daily rate and a cheaper weekly one. The form prices the dates a renter picks, then adds delivery or a fuel refill as its own line on the agreement.
fields.feature_3:
Condition photos at pickup and return

Staff photograph each item as it leaves and again when it comes back, and both sets sit on the rental record. A new dent or crack shows up before the deposit goes back.
fields.feature_4:
Insurance and operator details up front

Ask for a certificate of insurance upload and the name of whoever will run the machine. An agreement missing either one stays on hold until someone on your staff reviews it.
fields.feature_5:
Every rental that is out or overdue

Each signed agreement becomes a row with its item and its return date. Sort the table by that date to see what comes back today, then filter to rentals already late.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can take anywhere

Export the full codebase to GitHub when you want the agreement inside your own booking site, or when a developer is ready to connect it to the inventory system you run.
fields.why_title: Why Run Equipment Rentals on Emergent?
fields.why_description: A template PDF gets printed, filled in by hand at the counter and filed. Nobody can search it when a damaged item comes back.

fields.tab_content_1:
No certificate on file, no excavator leaves the yard

Granite Hill Rentals releases no machine without proof of insurance. A contractor books a mini excavator for 3 days at $385 a day, $1,155 in all. He uploads his certificate of insurance and names the operator. The agreement stays on hold until the yard manager approves the certificate, then goes out for signature.
fields.tab_content_2:
One order for 120 chairs, 15 tables and a tent

Bellweather Party Rentals quotes every wedding on one form. The couple picks a 20x40 tent at $450, 120 chairs at $3 each and 15 tables at $12, and the agreement prices each line for a $990 total. A $200 damage deposit is collected through Stripe, and the Friday delivery is booked once they sign.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every lens is checked against its pickup photos

Each lens leaving Lumen Camera Rental is photographed next to its serial number at checkout. When it comes back, staff take the same shots and the record shows both sets side by side. A scratched front element costs $120, taken out of the $500 deposit, and the renter gets $380 back.
fields.tab_content_4:
Tools back after 5 pm cost one more day

At the Oakline Hardware tool counter, rentals are due back by 5 pm. Each renter gets an email at 3 pm on the due date with the return time. A floor sander that comes back at 6:15 pm is charged one extra day at $68, added to that renter's agreement.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Equipment Rental Form
fields.howto_description: Get your inventory and your terms in order before you describe the form.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List each item as your yard tags it
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Price the extras before anyone asks
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide what the renter must prove
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write the damage and deposit terms
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every item you rent under the name your staff use on the floor, next to its tag number. Note what each one would cost to replace. The agreement pulls these details in, and renters never type a serial number themselves.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide what a delivery costs and what a fuel refill costs, and write each down as a fixed price. Settle the late fee now too. A charge agreed in advance is one nobody argues about when the equipment comes back.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick what has to be on file before an item leaves, such as a driver's license, a certificate of insurance or a named operator. Mark which items need which. A pressure washer needs far less paperwork than a skid steer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: State the deposit for each item and what can come out of it, such as damage beyond normal wear or a missing part. Have a lawyer review the wording for your state before the first renter signs it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put your item list and your rental terms into one prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the agreement form and the rentals table behind it. When you add a machine or change a rate, ask for the change in the same chat.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect Stripe to take deposits when the renter signs, and email to send return reminders. Anything else with an API, such as your accounting tool, can receive each signed agreement and each rental once it closes.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book a real item through the form on your phone. Upload a test certificate, sign, then check the item back in with photos. Confirm the deposit math is right and the agreement lands in the table with the correct return date.

claims_to_source: An equipment rental agreement typically identifies the owner and renter, describes the equipment (make, model, serial number), and states the rental period, fees, security deposit, and the renter's responsibility for damage or loss
Short-term equipment rentals usually run days, weeks or months and rarely go beyond a year, while longer arrangements are often structured as leases
Some rental companies require a certificate of insurance before they release certain equipment
